missed_quarantine: 'A flux vector of zeros gives NaN widths' should be wrong-result, not limitation: fbaSolution.v = zeros(n,1) is a valid documented 'n x 1 flux vector' (l.26-28), yet l.53 computes 0/0 = NaN, none of the bands l.56-61 match NaN, and l.74 stores NaN as the width of every model reaction in the map; the code's evident intent (l.61: ratio < 1e-3 -> width 1; l.72: default width 1) is contradicted. The sibling addFluxWidthAndColor guards exactly this case (its l.55-56 'Avoid division by zero if maxAbsFlux is zero').
why: Test assertions themselves are sound and hand-derived (bands, colour order, TOMATO then DARKTURQUOISE overwrite of molecule b, R4 not in model -> width 1). But the recorded severities are too low. Trigger to reproduce: map.rxnName={'R1';'R2'} (with the other documented fields as in the test), model.rxns={'R1';'R2'}, fbaSolution.v=[0;0]; [m]=addFluxFBAdirectionAndColor(map,model,fbaSolution); m.rxnWidth is {NaN;NaN}, expected {1;1}. The second recorded defect (ratio exactly 1e-3 keeps width 0.001 because l.60 is '> 1e-3' and l.61 is '< 1e-3') also contradicts the evident banding intent on a valid input (v=[1e-3;1] -> width 0.001 for R1), so by the rule it is wrong-result too, not cosmetic.
suggestion: Quarantine the function for the zero-vector NaN widths (wrong-result, l.53) and regrade the 1e-3 boundary entry (l.60-61) to wrong-result.

missed_quarantine: Species removal ignores modifiers, which gives a wrong-result on a valid map: removeCDReactions(file, {'R5'}) on the test's toy map extended with R5: E -> F (re5, base reactant s5/sa5, product a new species) while E (s5, sa5) still catalyses the kept R1. map.sID/map.sAlias from getMapMatrices hold only reactants and products (getMapMatrices l.71-108), so getCorrespondingRows(...,'exclusive') at l.62 and l.65 finds s5/sa5 used only by R5 and l.71 and l.74-75 delete them; the written _subset.xml still has R1's modification modifiers="s5" aliases="sa5" and its listOfModifiers reference, i.e. dangling references to a deleted species. This contradicts the header ('also removing corresponding species and species aliases if necessary', l.2-3): removing a species a remaining reaction uses is not 'necessary'. The recorded mirror case (modifier-only species E kept after removing R1, graded limitation) also contradicts the comment at l.37-38 ('to be able to delete isolated species and species aliases'), so by the rule it is wrong-result as well.
why: Assertions are hand-derived and correct for the reactant/product cases the fixture uses (R3 removal drops s4/sa4, R2 removal drops nothing, unknown names only). But the fixture never puts a species that is a reactant/product of a removed reaction and a modifier of a kept one, which is where the sID-based selection (l.62, l.65) corrupts the output, and the recorded modifier-only defect is graded too low.
suggestion: Quarantine for the dangling-modifier wrong-result (l.62/65/71/75); regrade the recorded 'modifier-only species kept' entry to wrong-result (evident intent l.37-38). If kept as a tested function, add a fixture with a species that is both a removed reaction's reactant and a kept reaction's modifier.

missed_quarantine: The entry 'Map information can be added or changed but not removed' is a wrong-result, not a limitation, at least for reversibility: [x,m]=transformXML2Map(f) on a file with <reaction ... reversible="false">; m.rxnReversibility{1}='true' (a value the header documents, l.40 "'false'/'true'", and exactly what transformToReversibleMap writes); transformMap2XML(x,m,out); [~,m2]=transformXML2Map(out) gives m2.rxnReversibility{1}='false'. l.162-164 write the attribute only when it is 'false', so the old reversible="false" stays, contradicting the documented result 'this information is then transferred to the xmlStruct' (l.19-20). Likewise emptied notes/compartment alias (l.79-81, 99-101, 281-283). Also the first recorded entry (l.108-109, 126-127: strcmp(alias, map.molAlias) used as an 'if' condition is true only when every alias equals it) is handling code that is never reached for a map of two or more aliases, so a reaction whose only reactant/product alias was removed is written with a dangling speciesReference instead of the intended error: wrong-result by the rule's 'handling code that is never reached' clause.
why: The assertions are hand-derived and thorough (round trip, edited values, removed alias sa6 dropped from multi-reference lists, single/no compartment, '~' path, error paths). The weakness is in grading: two recorded 'limitation' entries meet the wrong-result rule, and the edit section only edits rxnReversibility in the direction ('false') the code can write, so the failing direction ('true') is hidden.
suggestion: Quarantine for the l.162-164 reversibility transfer (wrong-result) and regrade the l.108-109/126-127 entry; if kept tested, add the 'true' reversibility edit, which would fail.

missed_quarantine: A custom setColours in the documented format fails with an index error (error severity, documented option): visualizeNormalizedRxnPresence(mapDir, {1,'aaaaaa',10; 0.5,'bbbbbb',5}) on the test's four maps (R4 present in none, fraction 0). For j=R4, i=2: 0 ~= 0.5, then l.150 reads setColours{3,1} -> 'Index in position 1 exceeds array bounds'. The header (l.28-32) documents setColours as rows {fraction, colour, line width} with an example list and never requires a final 0 row, so this is not an undocumented input. Secondary wrong-results: (a) the heatmap is saved into mapDir (l.169-170, as documented l.9-10) and every '*.xml' there is read as a map (l.67), so a second call on the same folder counts normalisedReactionHeatmap.xml as a map (its colours are not FFFF4500) and divides by n+1 (l.134): R1 present in all 4 maps gets 4/5=0.8 -> the (0.7,0.9] colour instead of the fraction-1 colour; the test deletes the heatmap before its second call (test l.127) and so hides this; (b) presence is a case-sensitive strcmp with 'FFFF4500' (l.101, l.117) while hex colour codes are case-insensitive and CellDesigner writes them lower case, so a valid map saved by CellDesigner counts no reaction as present (recorded as limitation; contradicts the evident intent of extracting reactions of that colour).
why: The assertions are hand-derived and correct for the cases they test (presence table, default and custom schemes with a 0 row, exact and range matches). Weaknesses: the second section deletes the previous heatmap so the documented 'saved in the directory with the XML files used to create it' + re-run behaviour is hidden, and the custom scheme always includes a 0 row, hiding the documented-option failure at l.150.
suggestion: Quarantine for the l.150 index error with a documented custom scheme (error); also record the re-run miscount (l.67/l.134/l.170) and regrade the lower-case colour entry to wrong-result.
